steps.domain_action: The initial conceptualization of the strychnine target in 1954.
Identification of the heptacyclic core as the primary structural challenge.
Retrosynthetic disconnection of the amide and ether linkages.
Disconnection of the target into the isostrychnine precursor and final reagents.
Identification of isostrychnine as a viable penultimate intermediate.
Further disconnection of isostrychnine into the Wieland-Gumlich aldehyde.
Disconnection of the indole and piperidine rings into simpler aromatic precursors.
Rejection of direct cyclization routes due to steric hindrance.
Identification of the veratraldehyde and o-toluidine starting materials.
Condensation of starting materials to form the initial Schiff base.
Successful formation of the first carbon-carbon bond.
Sequential addition of the malonic ester and subsequent cyclizations.
Permanent record of the crystalline intermediate at the relay point.
Branching into stereoisomeric possibilities during the Dieckmann condensation.
Simultaneous existence of diastereomers before resolution.
Selection of the correct stereocenter configuration.
Reconstitution of the tetracyclic core through ring closure.
Progression through the Woodward-Brehm intermediate.
Forward synthesis toward the isostrychnine framework.
Final coupling of the isostrychnine precursors.
Verification of the synthetic product against natural strychnine properties.
Final characterization and publication of the total synthesis.
Completion of the strychnine molecular boundary.
